This section is under development (draft). The developer’s personal data is not stored anywhere in the app.

APU does not charge anything and does not store payment data: the reminder is an ordinary local notification and goes nowhere. You make the transfer yourself in your bank; there too, if you want, you can set it up as a regular payment (auto-pay).
You can refresh the list by closing and reopening this screen.
Planned: bank transfer via SBP, card transfer, and crypto donations for people outside Russia.

Support is voluntary and changes nothing: all features are the same for everyone.
Donations go to: relays for connectivity on complex networks, storage of backups, GIF search, and work on the app.

There are no subscriptions, ads, or data sales inside. The app is distributed directly, bypassing app stores, so there are no in-app purchases. Every donation reaches the developer in full: a store would keep 15–30%. A direct donation is the most effective way to support the project, with no middlemen.
The app sets no file size limit. Actual transfer depends on free space, device capabilities, and the available network.

An invitation counts when your friend has installed the app via your link, added you to their contacts, and your messages have reached each other. Only people you invited yourself count. A rank received with a promo code counts the same as an earned one.

VIP is APU’s elite: your rank is no lower than “Pathfinder” (10th). The badge and the gold ring appear next to your name and avatar in chats, groups, and channels. The app’s features unlock with ranks.

No observations yet. The rating will appear by itself once the phone has been online and exchanged data with others.

The APU network is held up by the phones themselves. The more often a node is online, the faster it accepts files and the easier it is to connect to directly, the higher its rating — and the sooner data is sent to it. A declared space for relaying adds up to 10 points, and only for those who are online.

How much space the phone gives to data in transit: file chunks, other people’s files stored for contacts who are offline, and what waits for offline nodes. Here the phone acts as a server: the more space you give, the higher your rating with other nodes (up to +10 out of 100, and only while you are online).

Off — subscriber mode: NEW files from others are not accepted for storage, and heavy ones (pictures, videos, GIFs, large files) are not relayed to others. Light and essential traffic is carried by everyone: small documents and stickers, text and backups, update APKs.
The phone stores other people’s files for contacts who are offline, shares files of communities and updates with others. The more phone-servers there are, the faster the network is.
